source_text: Si aspersum fuerit sanguis super vestimentum, lavabis in loco sancto. Macula oratione et lacrimis lavatur.
thought_title: Washing the blood-stained garment in the holy place
orientation: Origen is interpreting Leviticus 6:27 about contact with sacrificial blood, now applying the rule about blood sprinkled on a garment to the cleansing of the soul.
pass_a_gloss: If [it] will have been sprinkled [with] blood upon [a] garment, you will wash [it] in [a] holy place. [A] stain by prayer and tears is washed.

choices.why: The future indicative carries the force of a command in the Latin rendering of the Levitical rule; kept as a directive.
The glossary term sanctus is rendered 'holy'; the phrase preserves the ritual location required by the law.
Rendered literally as 'stain' to preserve the image of a spot on a garment that must be cleansed, which Origen applies to the soul.
The passive present conveys the ongoing or general truth that the stain is removed by these means; 'washed away' captures the cleansing force.

bible_refs.note: Si aspersum fuerit sanguis super vestimentum, lavabis in loco sancto

pass_b_english: If blood has been sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash it in the holy place (Leviticus 6:27). A stain is washed away by prayer and tears.

last_rejected.quote: A stain is washed away by prayer and tears.
last_rejected.why: Source is Origen's commentary, not Scripture; English lacks marking that this is author's voice.
last_rejected.fix: The stain, he says, is washed away by prayer and tears.
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly renders 'Macula oratione et lacrimis lavatur' as author's commentary; no Scripture attribution in source.

last_rejected.why: English omits 'in loco sancto' / 'in the holy place' from the commentary clause, losing the spiritual location.
last_rejected.fix: A stain is washed away by prayer and tears in the holy place.
last_rejected.ruling: 'in loco sancto' belongs to Leviticus quote, correctly translated; commentary clause 'Macula...lavatur' lacks it.
